promises.promise: An outside program has one door: the API, with a token. The command line, the web app, agents and anything outside loom call the same operations through the same permission check.
One API for the command line, the web app and agents.
A token says who is calling and what it may reach.
Someone else's program sees only what a household owner granted it.
The phone and any other interface are callers like any other.
A token belongs to one member, one agent or one machine.
Every part's operations are reached the same way.
The labels on each record decide what this caller may reach.
The live connection is how a caller gets rows and then changes.
A runner sees and reports only the jobs assigned to it.
Anything outside loom calls the API with a token. Someone else's program is a caller with a token: it sees only the record types and operations a household owner granted it.
There is one loom per home: one program and one data folder. Beyond Node and npm nothing is required. A restart is an acceptable deploy.

Each part is a module with a declared, typed interface. A role has one implementation at a time, so replacing the task store means writing another module that fills the tasks role. A bridge is replaced the same way.
The phone does what the desk does, built after the desk is right. It is a caller like any other.
a Checked here. Permission is checked where something outside calls the API, and nowhere else.
b Installed means trusted. Loom's own parts never ask each other for permission.

c The rule. A household owner sees everything, including what is private to another member. Anyone else sees what is in their projects, plus what belongs to agents they own. Private to a member means that member plus household owners.
